messages:
rachel: Heads-up — planning a base-image rebuild Wed 02:00 UTC. Main changes: switch to distroless base, prune glibc, and rotate cosign/KMS keys. Need RBAC review for signing service accounts and clear audit-log expectations. @lucas can you confirm current signer SA scope?
lucas: In staging signer-sa has storage.objectViewer + iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator because CI impersonates. In prod we gave storage.objectViewer + roles/cloudkms.signer only. Question: does the deploy pipeline still rely on tokenCreator?
sam: Which flow? If CI does SA impersonation (impersonate the signer SA), tokenCreator is required on the runner. If we switch to KMS-backed cosign, we can avoid tokenCreator and instead grant the runner iam.serviceAccountUser to impersonate a limited gate runner.
maya: Also: compliance needs image-sign audit records in our centralized index. KMS emits key-use logs but we should also emit a structured attestation record to GCS/BigQuery with fields: image_digest, signer_subject, kms_key_id, infra_run_id, commit_sha. ops-bot, do we have a skeleton?
ops-bot: audit-template: https://internal.redwood/audit/templates/image-sign.json — fields: [image_digest, signer_subject, kms_key_id, infra_run_id, commit_sha, cosign_version]
lucas: Current pipeline calls cosign like this:
```
cosign sign --key gcpkms://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/rebuild/cryptoKeys/cosignKey \
  docker.io/redwood/runtime:sha256:abcdef
```
rachel: Rotation question: when we rotate KMS keys, how do verifiers handle older signatures? We need a keyset metadata annotation in image manifest or attestations to map which pubkeys verify which images. Thinking `redwood.com/signer-keyset:v1` annotation with KMS key version refs.
sam: We already push per-image attestations to GCS in prod, but verifier currently only checks manifest annotations for `cosign.sigstore.dev`. If we add explicit keyset metadata and include `signed_by: [kms://.../cryptoKeyVersions/1]` we can skip expensive KMS discovery at verify time.
lucas: RBAC detail: who should be able to view key metadata? Proposal: security-readers + SRE-oncall read access. Signing rights should be extremely limited: only the signing-runner SA (allowlist) and a small signer-operator group. No developer accounts in prod.
rachel: Also require conditional bindings (MFA + source IP from build pool) for any principal with cosign signing privileges. And log any `cryptoKeyVersions.*.asymmetricSign` calls.
maya: Incident playbook draft for key compromise: 1) revoke key version (mark DO_NOT_USE), 2) add compromised key to verifier denylist, 3) re-sign critical base images with new key, 4) deploy verifier rollout canary to 5% then 100%, 5) notify customers + compliance. Need runbook edits and a tabletop. @sam can you draft?
sam: Will draft incident playbook and add checklist entries to the rebuild doc. ETA: EOD tomorrow.
lucas: Small change I'm going to test now: remove iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator from prod signer-sa and validate the pipeline still signs by using KMS-backed cosign via the runner SA impersonation. Will report blockers here.
maya: Retention: compliance requires 2y for image sign/audit logs. KMS and GCS currently 90d. ops-bot can you open a ticket to sink logs to long-term bucket with 730d TTL?
ops-bot: Created SECG-4823: sink audit logs -> gs://redwood-audit-longterm, TTL=730d, owners: security, eng-infra.
rachel: OK — I'll update the base-image rebuild checklist to include: RBAC review snapshot, audit-template usage, key rotation compatibility, verifier keyset annotation, verifier-canary plan, and link to the incident playbook once Sam drafts it.
lucas: quick FYI: I'll also add a manifest annotation example to the pipeline: `annotations: {"redwood.com/signer-keyset": "gcpkms://projects/.../cryptoKeyVersions/1"}` and drop tokenCreator from prod signer-sa if tests pass.
sam: :thumbsup:
